extracted.intended_audience: academic peer reviewers and authors preparing or evaluating scholarly manuscripts (broad research disciplines; users of F1000Research-style open peer review)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and exemplars for writing and assessing peer reviews and for authors preparing manuscripts (includes statistical critique, data-publication commentary, software/package papers, negative-replication studies, and clinical case reports). Emphasizes correctness, clarity, reproducibility, and appropriate scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness of statistical analysis and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses and conclusions must be mathematically and conceptually correct (e.g., correct computation of posterior probabilities, correct interpretation of likelihoods and priors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: distinguish when Efron (2013a) gives 2/3 as the correct posterior vs incorrect claims; check algebra, logic, and published corrections; explicitly point out incorrect statements and why they are wrong. Use concrete demonstrations (e.g., worked examples, MCMC code) to verify claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish uncertainty about a particular state vs population-level parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly separate uncertainty about a single instance (the state of this set of twins) from uncertainty about population-frequency parameters (the prior distribution for Pr(x=1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain which parameter the data inform. Note that a sample of size one (especially biased) is informative about that instance but weak or biased for population-frequency estimation; avoid conflating these levels of inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate specification and justification of priors
rubrics_metrics.description: Priors must be logically constructed and their implications for inference explained (e.g., fixed-value prior vs uninformative priors such as dunif(0,1) or dbeta(0.5,0.5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss the mean of the prior, whether it implies a prior probability for the instance, and how different priors affect posterior distributions; justify choice of prior and note when different priors yield the same inference for the quantity of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use data correctly to update prior beliefs (Bayesian updating)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an analysis claims Bayesian updating, show how data change the prior to posterior for the parameter of interest (e.g., show Pr(x=1|y=1) ≠ Pr(x=1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the updating equation or code (e.g., WinBUGS snippet/MCMC) and demonstrate the posterior; flag claims that there are 'no data' when a data point does update the prior for the instance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of sample bias and sample-size limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge when data are a biased sample and when small sample size (n=1) undermines population inference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why a biased single observation is not a firm basis for estimating population parameters, and discuss implications for interpretation and robustness of conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify Bayesian results with frequentist or alternative checks when informative
rubrics_metrics.description: Where priors are uncertain, consider cross-checks (e.g., likelihood weighting, frequentist assessment of evidence) to provide perspective on conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: show likelihoods under competing hypotheses and compute scaled weights (Burnham & Anderson 2002) to compare with uninformative-prior posteriors; note limitations of checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reproducible methodological details and code
rubrics_metrics.description: Include code, model specification, or other technical details sufficient to reproduce statistical results (e.g., WinBUGS code, MCMC settings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share runnable scripts or clear model blocks; use them to demonstrate posterior quantities claimed in the manuscript and to allow verification of claims by reviewers/readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate use of terminology and data description
rubrics_metrics.description: Report and interpret observed data precisely (e.g., distinguish 'twins are both male' from 'twins are fraternal'), and ensure statements about the data match the analysis question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag incorrect characterizations of the data that make calculations irrelevant; clarify what is observed versus what is being inferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about perspective, scope, and definitions in opinion pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Opinion essays should explicitly state the authors' viewpoint and define key terms (e.g., what 'data publication' means to them).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether the authors accept particular definitions (e.g., Lawrence et al.), the intended scope, and what parts of the problem are outside the essay's remit; make implied positions explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a comprehensive and defensible typology when categorizing models
rubrics_metrics.description: When classifying models (e.g., types of data publication), avoid oversimplification and examine whether proposed categories capture real-world complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the 'other' category in depth, include more examples (beyond Zenodo/Figshare), and consider subtypes such as domain vs institutional repositories or publisher roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine validation mechanisms beyond conventional peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider alternative validation approaches (technical, scientific, team-based curation) and identify appropriate validators beyond conventional peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss roles for curators, data scientists, repository teams, and who is responsible for which aspects of validation; consider formalizing team-based processes as alternatives/complements to peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critically analyze incentive and credit mechanisms for data sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether citation and data-publication models actually incentivize sharing and stewardship and consider alternative incentive designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask who needs to be incentivized, for what behaviors, and whether current citation-based credit systems are effective; draw on evidence or propose testable alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear takeaways and recommended next steps in opinion/review pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclude with a summary, suggested directions, immediate challenges, or calls to action rather than ending abruptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the main takeaway, list actionable recommendations or things to stop/start doing, and indicate priorities for research or policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough copy-editing and adherence to style/grammar conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be free of typos, grammatical errors, and misuses of terminology (e.g., 'data' as plural).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request a quick copy edit for typos, missing words, wrong verb tenses, and consistent usage (e.g., NSIDC vs NSICD); flag language that impedes comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate and complete attribution of collaborative efforts and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge all relevant organizations and prior work accurately (e.g., contributors to joint declarations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add footnotes or references listing participating organizations where appropriate; avoid implying a single leader when efforts were joint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement deep citation and structural indexing for subsets of data
rubrics_metrics.description: Deep citation should identify a structural index (e.g., space/time, gene sequence position, variable) to reference subsets precisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend using structural indices appropriate to the domain (space/time in Earth science, gene sequence positions in genomics) and discuss implications for identifiers and subset citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overstating claims about repository practices without evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: When asserting that few repositories provide scientific review, verify this claim and acknowledge documented examples of repositories that do perform scientific review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete examples and documentation (e.g., PDS, tDAR) and characterize common team-based validation practices rather than assuming rarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize reproducibility in software/package papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Software manuscripts should highlight reproducibility of workflows and demonstrate how the package supports reproducible science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include practical examples, vignettes, or appendices showing reproducible pipelines; emphasize reproducibility as a key feature and assess adequacy of examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent and user-friendly API and function naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Package function names should be consistent, concise, and user-friendly; avoid long names and inconsistent naming conventions across data sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider generic function names with a connection/object abstraction (e.g., taxizeDB + search(foo, 'Abies')) to reduce proliferation of source-specific function names and improve learnability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript code and output presentation should be clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate code inputs from outputs clearly in the manuscript so readers can easily parse examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demarcate outputs (use conventional notations or whitespace), separate input/output code chunks, and avoid mixing R prompts with printed output that confuses readers unfamiliar with the language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain consistency in naming conventions across outputs and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Column names, object names, and case conventions should be consistent (avoid mixing camelCase and snake_case without reason).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardize naming early in the manuscript and package; note inconsistencies (e.g., 'matched_name' vs 'data_source_title' vs camelCase) and correct them for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure examples and printed outputs accurately reflect inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples in the paper must be correct and internally consistent (the printed outputs should correspond to the inputs shown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check example inputs and resulting outputs; correct mismatches such as misspelt taxa in example vectors or outputs that appear inconsistent with the declared input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use unique figure numbering and distinguish appendix figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures in appendices should be numbered and referenced distinctly from main-text figures to avoid duplicate figure numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renumber appendix figures (e.g., Appendix Figure 1, 2) or use a prefix to prevent duplicated Figure 1 labels and to avoid reader confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize plot aesthetics and include appropriate scales/legends
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should have appropriate point sizes, transparency, scales, and legends so that graphical density and relationships are interpretable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust plotting-character size for transparency effects, include axes/scales for phylogenetic trees if conventionally required, and follow plotting conventions to facilitate interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and clarity in domain-specific nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: Use correct biological/technical terms and formatting (e.g., 'Argonaute' not 'Argonate'; correct miRNA naming and avoid splitting miRNA across line breaks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure domain-specific nomenclature conforms to community standards and is consistently formatted; correct typographical issues introduced during typesetting that hamper understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient conceptual development of key topics in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Review articles should expand on important concepts (e.g., miRNA clusters, antagomir, patterns of downregulation in disease) and provide deeper analysis rather than brief mentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify places where readers would benefit from expanded treatment and recommend including more background, mechanistic discussion, or literature evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include appropriate positive and methodological controls in replication/negative-result studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure-to-reproduce papers need additional controls (positive controls, spectral confirmation, assay sensitivity) to strengthen claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: include emission spectra to distinguish autofluorescence from GFP, qPCR positive control samples (mESC/miPSC) to show assay sensitivity, and reprogramming efficiency comparisons using conventional methods; consider obtaining material from original authors for simultaneous analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract should accurately reflect content and specify important details
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles and abstracts must concisely and accurately summarize essential information and define key specifics (e.g., anatomical specificity in case reports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise abstracts to include clarifying details (e.g., 'mild mitral regurgitation' rather than generic 'valvulopathy') and place availability/URI information appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent reporting of clinical/laboratory data and resolution of inconsistencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolve discrepancies in reported measurements (e.g., prolactin levels), clarify timeline and figure dates, and report whether baseline measurements were taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When discrepancies appear (e.g., 'prolactin >1000' vs '55 ng/ml'), explain causes (hook effect) or label as limitations; clarify figure timepoints and whether baseline echocardiography was performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare limitations when baseline or reference data are missing
rubrics_metrics.description: If pre-treatment or baseline measurements were not obtained, explicitly state this as a limitation in the Discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge missing baseline data and discuss how this affects interpretation and the study's conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain clinical measurement changes and ensure measurement consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: When clinical values change over time (e.g., LV ejection fraction), provide plausible explanations and indicate whether the same measurement method was used across timepoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss potential reasons for observed changes (treatment switches, measurement variability) and confirm consistent measurement techniques to support the interpretation.
